claim: Propranolol can alter later conditioned fear expression when paired with memory reactivation
rationale: Multiple human studies and 2026 systematic review support a laboratory effect but modality/paradigm inconsistency remains

claim: Propranolol plus trauma-memory reactivation reduces PTSD symptoms more than placebo
rationale: Brunet positive signal conflicts with Roullet null and 2022 vs 2025 meta-analytic conclusions; clinical effect remains uncertain

claim: Retrieval-extinction reliably prevents return of conditioned fear in humans
rationale: Influential positive original result is weakened by reanalysis and negative preregistered replication

claim: Prediction error is a relevant moderator of post-retrieval fear-memory updating
rationale: Several studies support PE relevance but precise boundary rules have failed replication and operationalizations vary

claim: A single prediction error universally triggers fear-memory destabilization
rationale: Direct failed replication and null PE-type studies argue against a universal one-PE rule

claim: Memory strength moderates retrieval-extinction/reconsolidation effects in humans
rationale: New 2025 direct study is relevant but independent replication and full effect extraction are lacking

claim: PTSD symptom improvement after reactivation demonstrates reconsolidation as the mechanism
rationale: Clinical symptom change does not isolate reconsolidation from exposure extinction expectancy contact or nonspecific pharmacology

claim: DCS produces a small average augmentation of exposure-based therapy across anxiety OCD PTSD
rationale: IPD meta-analysis shows a small average effect but protocols diagnoses and timing vary

claim: DCS provides a consistent clinical benefit specifically in PTSD exposure therapy
rationale: PTSD trials include positive negative and null findings; larger multisite trial found no stable main effect

claim: FAAH inhibition increases anandamide in humans
rationale: Direct pharmacodynamic target engagement shown in experimental medicine and PTSD trial

claim: FAAH inhibition improves delayed extinction recall in healthy humans
rationale: Controlled experimental-medicine signal but limited independent replication

claim: FAAH inhibition improves exposure-based CBT outcomes in PTSD
rationale: Direct N=100 randomized trial was negative despite increased anandamide

claim: Acute sodium butyrate improves later extinction-memory retrieval in healthy humans
rationale: Single N=180 triple-blind RCT reported a 7-day expectancy benefit only after robust/high-trial extinction; no corresponding clear skin-conductance effect or prevention of reinstatement; effect estimates and independent clinical replication remain unavailable

claim: Butyrate prevents return of fear or reinstatement in humans
rationale: The 2026 human trial did not prevent reinstatement

claim: Butyrate improves clinical PTSD exposure therapy
rationale: No direct clinical PTSD efficacy trial identified in the current corpus

claim: Post-extinction L-DOPA reliably improves human extinction retrieval
rationale: Earlier positive findings were not confirmed as a significant main effect in a preregistered 2024 replication

claim: Post-extinction L-DOPA reduces some return-of-fear measures in PTSD
rationale: Single PTSD laboratory study showed reduced reinstatement but no improved extinction recall

claim: L-DOPA improves clinical PTSD treatment outcomes
rationale: No established clinical augmentation efficacy

claim: Intranasal oxytocin reliably improves human fear extinction
rationale: Human findings are directionally inconsistent and a larger 2025 RCT found impaired extinction learning

claim: Oxytocin improves Prolonged Exposure outcomes in PTSD
rationale: Small pilot was feasible but symptom differences were not statistically significant

claim: Lurasidone improves extinction-related behavior in selected animal models
rationale: Rodent SERT-KO and procognitive studies support a preclinical signal

claim: Lurasidone improves human fear extinction or PTSD exposure learning
rationale: No direct controlled human fear-extinction/PTSD augmentation evidence identified

claim: Explicitly focusing on expectancy violation improves immediate exposure outcomes in PTSD
outcome: fear responses and PTSD symptoms at one week
rationale: One small randomized experiment (N=60) found no between-condition differences in fear responses or PTSD symptoms at one week; numeric estimates and precision were not extracted, and longer-term benefit remains untested.
